articles.title: Who Is Ashoke Sen? The Kolkata Physicist Who Unified String Theory — and Just Became the First Indian to Win the Oskar Klein Medal
articles.excerpt: He did his apprenticeship at Fermilab and Stanford, then chose in 1988 to build his career in India. Four decades later, Ashoke Sen — Breakthrough Prize laureate, Dirac medallist, Fellow of the Royal Society at 42 — has received Stockholm's Oskar Klein Medal, an honour no Indian physicist had won in its 38 years.
articles.image_caption: Theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen in the Physics department of Scottish Church College, Kolkata, in 2019. Sen received the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal in Stockholm, becoming the first Indian physicist to win the honour.
articles.nri_angle: Sen is the diaspora's reverse-migration archetype: Stony Brook PhD, Fermilab and Stanford postdocs, then a deliberate 1988 return to India — proof, over 38 years and physics' highest honours, that world-first science can be built from Indian institutions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
